analysis.title: Yelp Inc. (YELP) Q3'26 Review: Product-Led Growth Strategy on Display Despite Persistent Macro Headwinds
key_insights: GS maintains Neutral on YELP and cuts the 12-month price target to $23 from $24. Price was $20.52 on 5 Nov 2026, implying 12.1% upside.
Q3'26 total revenue was $371mm, 1% above GS ($368mm) and Visible Alpha consensus ($369mm) and above the $365-370mm guidance range. Revenue was down 1% YoY.

Other revenue grew 82% YoY to $34mm and was the driver of the beat. Management reiterated its path to exiting 2028 at a $250mm annualized run rate, as Yelp diversifies across transactions, subscriptions and data licensing.

Core Advertising revenue was $337mm, down 6% YoY, with declines in both Services (-2% YoY) and Restaurants, Retail & Other (RR&O, -13% YoY). GS attributes this to persistent macro pressure on consumer and advertiser spend.
Services Paid Advertising Locations (PALs) fell 5% below GS at 248K (-4% QoQ, -4% YoY). RR&O revenue per PAL was $378, down 15% YoY.
Adj. EBITDA was $92mm (24.9% margin), 25% above GS and 24% above consensus, and above the $70-75mm guidance. GAAP EPS was $0.63 vs GS $0.43 and consensus $0.44.
Management modestly lowered its FY26 total revenue guidance, citing a challenging macro environment for consumers and local businesses. FY26 revenue guidance is now $1,455-1,460mm.

Management plans to lean into investment in product and sales/go-to-market for long-term initiatives (Hatch, Yelp Host and others) despite near-term topline headwinds. GS says this may pressure FY27 margins.
Product velocity increased in Q3, with voice AI integrated in Hatch, a new OpenTable integration and more personalization in Yelp Assistant. Yelp is positioning to benefit from rising AI adoption.
Stock-based compensation (SBC) is expected to fall below 6% of revenue in Q4, one year ahead of prior guidance.

GS cut Q4'26 estimates to revenue of $350mm (from $362mm), adj. EBITDA of $60mm (from $76mm) and GAAP EPS of $0.29 (from $0.50). 2027 estimates are now revenue of $1.47bn (from $1.49bn), adj. EBITDA of $302mm (from $312mm) and GAAP EPS of $1.91 (from $2.13).

GS expects investor debate to center on how macro headwinds and the pace of management's investment spending shape revenue growth and margins into 2027. Long-term, GS is watching whether new revenue lines produce more sustainable growth away from core Advertising.

The $23 target blends two methods equally: 5.5x EV/GAAP EBITDA (unchanged) on NTM+1 estimates, and a modified DCF at 7.5x EV/FCF-SBC (from 9.0x) on NTM+4 estimates, discounted 3 years at 12%. Scenario values are $13 downside, $23 base and $30 upside.
YELP is down 20.1% over 3 months, 29.8% over 6 months and 36.2% over 12 months. Relative to the Russell 2000 it is down 11.7%, 26.8% and 42.4% over the same windows. Market cap is $1.1bn.

market_movers.rationale: GS lowers its target from $24 to $23 on lower operating estimates and updated management commentary. The 7.5x EV/FCF-SBC multiple replaces 9.0x. The rating has been Neutral since Oct 13, 2024.

earnings_insights: YELP Q3'26 reported 11/5/2026: total revenue $371mm vs GS est $368mm and consensus $369mm, guidance $365-370mm. Revenue -1% YoY.
YELP Q3'26 reported GAAP EPS $0.63 vs GS est $0.43 and consensus $0.44. GAAP EBITDA was $66mm (17.9% margin) vs consensus $50mm.
YELP Q3'26 reported adj. EBITDA $92mm (24.9% margin) vs GS est $74mm, consensus $74mm and guidance $70-75mm.

YELP Q3'26 reported Advertising revenue $337mm (-6% YoY): Services $238mm (-2% YoY, 1% above consensus), RR&O $99mm (-13% YoY, 2% above consensus). Other revenue was $34mm (+82% YoY), 5% below consensus.
YELP Q3'26 reported total PALs 509K (-1% YoY). Services PALs were 248K (-4% YoY), RR&O PALs 261K (+3% YoY). Total revenue per PAL was $662 (-5% YoY).

YELP Q4'26 company guidance: revenue $347-352mm and adj. EBITDA $57-62mm. GS estimates are revenue $350mm and adj. EBITDA $60mm (prior $362mm and $76mm). GS adj. EPS est is $0.67 (prior $0.92) and GAAP EPS est $0.29 (prior $0.50).

YELP FY26 GS estimates: revenue $1,457mm (prior $1,467mm, guidance $1,455-1,460mm), adj. EBITDA $323mm (guidance $320-325mm), adj. EPS $3.56 (prior $3.60), GAAP EPS $1.78. Advertising revenue is raised 1.7% to $1,254mm while Services is cut 2.2% to $934mm.

YELP FY27 GS estimates: revenue $1,469mm (-1.4%), adj. EBITDA $302mm (-3.1%), adj. EPS $3.47 (from $3.75), GAAP EPS $1.91 (from $2.13). Adj. EBITDA margin is 20.5%. FY28 estimates are revenue $1,519mm, adj. EBITDA $331mm, adj. EPS $4.10.
risk_factors: Macro headwinds deviate from GS expectations, whether they last longer or recover faster, affecting PALs and ad spend growth, especially local.
User growth and engagement trends deviate from expectations, in core restaurant/retail or in newer home services use cases.
Management execution on key product initiatives (self-serve, multi-location, home services, Yelp Audiences) varies, with competition, advertiser/user adoption and internal execution as the variables.
Shareholder returns from share buybacks come in above or below expectations.
Investment in growth initiatives could pressure FY27 margins while topline remains weak.

tension_points.bull_case: Other revenue grew 82% YoY with a stated path to a $250mm annualized run rate exiting 2028. Product velocity is rising (Hatch voice AI, OpenTable integration), SBC is falling and adj. EBITDA beat guidance.
tension_points.bear_case: Core Advertising fell 6% YoY, FY26 revenue guidance was trimmed, and Services PALs are shrinking. Planned investment in product and go-to-market may pressure FY27 margins, and GS cut 2027 adj. EBITDA 3.1% and adj. EPS 7.4%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A faster or slower macro recovery than GS models would change the PAL and local ad spend outlook. Execution on self-serve, multi-location, home services and Yelp Audiences is the other swing factor.

theme_stances.key_argument: Other revenue is growing quickly, but core Advertising is declining under macro pressure, so GS stays Neutral.
theme_stances.evidence: We maintain our Neutral rating & adjust our PT from $24 to $23
